name: orion-api CI-CD
originalTriggers: push: main, release/* (not release/legacy-*), paths src, tests, Dockerfile (not docs, *.md), batch builds
pull request: main, release/* (docs excluded), autoCancel

extraAllowedHosts.why: The production health endpoint the Smoke test step calls; it is this plan's own service and no secret is in that step.

taskMap.github: run steps: dotnet restore, build, test (find over tests/**/*.csproj), publish + zip
taskMap.note: project globs are expanded with find/xargs

taskMap.github: docker/login-action + docker/build-push-action; docker/login-action again before the scan
taskMap.note: tags: build number and latest; the build number is date + run number, not Azure's $(Rev:.r) counter
runtimeStack DOTNETCORE|8.0 has no input in the action: set it on the web app

taskMap.github: azure/login (OIDC) + az in a run step

unsupported.reason: Azure shows a Tests tab with pass/fail history; no step in the allow-listed actions produces an equivalent view

unsupported.suggestion: upload to a coverage service or add a reviewed report action

templates.handledBy: inlined as the Restore local tools and Verify formatting steps
inlined as the Dependency vulnerability scan and Publish scan report steps (failOnHighSeverity true: no continue-on-error)

acceptedWarnings.why: The source gives these jobs no environment and keeps the credentials at repository level (Azure variable groups are not environment-scoped). Scoping them to a GitHub environment is a hardening choice for the reviewer; it would add approvals and deployment records the source does not have.

notes: NOT executed on GitHub: only linted by actionlint and zizmor and checked by the policy gates.

Environments dev and prod must be created in the repository; the source's prod approval (Release Managers, branch control main) and the OIDC trust for each Azure identity are configured there, not in this file. Repository-level secrets are the dev identity; the prod environment must override AZURE_* with the prod identity.

Group orion-keyvault-prod (db-admin-password, stripe-secret-key, signing-certificate) is linked to the prod stage but none of its variables is referenced by the YAML; its secret names are not valid GitHub secret names (hyphens) and nothing is created for them.
Non-secret variables of the linked groups are exported as workflow env, as Azure exposes them to script steps. Group secrets are not exposed implicitly, as in Azure.
The Docker@2 service connection orion-acr (a registry credential, not Azure) becomes the ORION_ACR_USERNAME/ORION_ACR_PASSWORD secrets; an OIDC login with az acr login would be safer.
The image scan assumes trivy exists on the runner; it is not installed by this workflow.
The ENABLE_SMOKE_TESTS pipeline variable is exported but, as in the source, nothing reads it; the SLACK_WEBHOOK secret variable is not referenced by the YAML and is not created.

The variables template pipelines/templates/variables.yml (not a step template, so the task analyser does not count it) is converted to workflow env: NUGET_PACKAGES now points inside the workspace instead of Pipeline.Workspace, DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT is kept, dotnetSdkVersion is unused as in the source.
